title: Oncall Navigator: Rapid Actions & Telemetry for Private Deployments
creator: Riley Chen
description: Design a compact, action-first Oncall Navigator panel for Redwood Private/VPC clusters that surfaces critical telemetry, contextual remediation steps, and one-tap safe actions for oncall engineers. The Navigator lives as a docked micro-panel in the Private Console cluster view and on the Operations page, optimized for fast decision-making during incidents and upgrades.
goals: Reduce mean time to mitigation for common private-cluster incidents (network flaps, node evictions, KV cache corruption)
Provide a single, scannable snapshot combining connectivity health, SLO deviations, and cost impact of remediation actions
Make safe, reversible operations (eg. soft-evict tenant, scaled drain, route failover) accessible with clear approvals and audit trails
scope: Design includes layout, interaction patterns for quick actions, telemetry widgets (latency spike strip, pod-level CPU/GPU sparkline, inter-region packet loss), playbook stepper, confirmation/approval flows, and cost-preview microcopy. Out of scope: backend implementation, RBAC policy enforcement details (assume existing RBAC primitives).
acceptance_criteria: Navigator dock appears on Private cluster detail page and Operations -> Incidents for clusters in scope
At-a-glance telemetry: cluster-level latency band, node drain status, network path health and recent failover count
Three safe quick actions available with inline cost impact preview and one mandatory reviewer approval: 'Soft Evict Tenant', 'Shift Traffic to Failover Region', 'Start Rolling Drain (safe)'
Playbook stepper shows canonical remediation steps and links to full runbook; each step can be marked as done and logged to the incident timeline
Design handoff artifacts (Figma spec, props table, microcopy) delivered and design review sign-off recorded
tradeoffs: Surface vs safety: exposing powerful actions reduces time-to-mitigation but increases risk; mitigations include mandatory reviewers, cooldowns, and audit-first UX
Density vs scannability: compact view must limit widgets; we prioritize SLO deviations and connectivity over exhaustive metrics
Cost-preview accuracy vs latency: on-demand cost estimate must be coarse (seconds) rather than exact to avoid blocking actions
review_feedback: PM (Diego Alvarez): prefer 'soft-evict' naming to avoid confusion with permanent eviction — update microcopy
SRE (Samir Patel): require explicit RBAC check indicator before quick actions are enabled; add tooltip linking to RBAC docs
